## Design rulings — Kev direct, 2026-10-20 ~9:33 AM CT
- DQ2 RESOLVED: throw-vs-sidestep stays POSITIONAL. A sidestep dodges a throw only by physically leaving grab range; no state-based throw whiff. Do not re-raise.
- LONG-TERM VISION: Street Dojo ultimately becomes a persistent open-world MMO mobile game. The current 1v1 fighter is the combat foundation. Design implication for the loop: prefer choices that do not paint the combat core into corners hostile to later networked, persistent, many-player play (deterministic-ish simulation, no hard-coded 1v1-only assumptions where a clean generalization costs nothing) — but do NOT slow the prototype or build MMO features now.

## KEV DIRECTIVE — EACH LEG SUPPORTS WEIGHT INDEPENDENTLY — 2026-10-21 ~02:21 CT
Kev, reviewing the current stance: "Right now you have both legs doing the same thing instead of each leg supporting body weight in a physically accurate manner."

Requirement (joins the 2026-10-21 08:00 cycle's stance pass, ahead of the R4 backdrop):
- Legs must NOT mirror each other. At any moment each leg has an independent role: SUPPORT (foot planted, knee near-straight, hip–ankle line under the body's center of mass, carrying the load) vs FREE (unloaded — may bend, lift, swing, or rest).
- Idle/guard: weight rests predominantly on ONE leg; the pelvis shifts toward the support side; the free leg relaxes (different knee angle and foot placement from the support leg). No 50/50 split with identical knee bends.
- Walking/striking: single-support phases — the pelvis/COM projects over the support foot (within a tolerance the cycle sets); the swing leg passes through bent and unloaded; strikes drive through the planted support leg.
- Measure before dispatch: extend probe_stance.js to report PER-LEG knee angles independently and pelvis-to-support-foot horizontal offset; set explicit acceptance (e.g., idle legs differ measurably in knee angle with pelvis offset toward the support foot; at walk mid-stance samples the support knee is straighter than the swing knee). Build on cycle 5's pelvis shift — note its known gap (hip anchors ignore pel[2], so legs don't follow the lateral shift yet): this directive is exactly that gap, now Kev-directed.

## QUEUE UPDATE — Kev directive 2026-10-26 ~10:16 CT (recorded by main agent)

Kev, on the DQ18b2/DQ18c/DQ18d progress: "Ok good. Continue." Then three additions:

- **NEW NEXT ITEM — DQ17j STANDING RECOVERY (takes priority over DQ18e).** After the DQ17i gradual get-up completes, the fighter does NOT snap back to full control. Add a stumble window (~24–36 frames):
  - The stumble is center-of-gravity driven: the pelvis/COM drifts toward and briefly past the edge of the support base; the fighter takes 1–3 short corrective steps in the direction of the drift, each step landing under the falling COM; arms reach/windmill for balance; knees stay soft; the stance is fully regained only at the window's end.
  - During the stumble the fighter cannot block or walk normally (vulnerable — that's the cost).
  - **Slight chance of a desperation strike:** with a small probability (~15%, a tunable constant) the fighter throws ONE strike from their own style set mid-stumble, at reduced power (~×0.6 damage/knockback), and the stumble extends slightly afterward (throwing it costs balance). If it doesn't fire, the stumble simply plays out.
  - Acceptance probe must measure: COM projection vs the support base (exits and recovers), corrective-step count and direction vs COM drift, desperation-strike rate over ≥200 trials inside a target band around the constant, joint-step continuity (no teleports), and full stance regained at window end.
- **DQ18e — MOVES + COMBINATIONS EXPANSION (follows DQ17j; alternates with fall refinement as before).** Keep adding different moves and combinations to both styles: more distinct strikes per style (e.g., RED: overhand / lunging hook class; BLUE: backfist / crescent-kick class — final picks at brief time) and longer mixed chains (hand→leg and leg→hand combos through the DQ18d buffer system), each new move at the DQ18b2 extension/contact standard.
- **STANDING ACCEPTANCE FOCUS — PHYSICS + CENTER OF GRAVITY (Kev, all future cycles).** Every new move, combo, fall, and recovery change must include center-of-gravity evidence in its acceptance probe: pelvis/COM position relative to the support foot/base through the motion, support-leg loading, and recovery of balance. A motion that looks right but carries impossible COM (COM far outside the base with no step, lunge, or fall to explain it) FAILS the cycle.

## QUEUE UPDATE — Kev directive 2026-10-26 ~10:20 CT (recorded by main agent)

Kev: "Figures should react relative to the power of the strike."

- **STANDING RULE — REACTION PROPORTIONALITY.** Every reaction a figure makes scales with the power of the specific strike that caused it — per MOVE, not just per class. DQ16 already scales knockback and stun recoil by class (P < K < L); this rule generalizes and deepens it. Each strike carries a power value (boxing: jab < cross < hook < uppercut; kung fu: palm < straight < chop, kicks/sweep per their class; launcher highest), and the following must all be monotonic in that power: hitstun duration, recoil distance and head/body snap, stagger depth, whether a hit launches vs staggers (and fall intensity when it does), get-up time, and standing-recovery stumble severity (below). A jab must visibly move a figure less than an uppercut in every one of these channels.
- **AMENDMENT to DQ17j (standing recovery, next cycle):** stumble severity scales with the power of the strike that caused the knockdown — a light-strike knockdown gives a short, shallow stumble; a launcher knockdown gives a longer stumble with more corrective steps and deeper COM excursions. The desperation-strike chance stays slight across the board.
- **NEW ITEM — DQ19 REACTION PROPORTIONALITY PASS (after DQ17j, before DQ18e expansion continues).** Audit every reaction channel against per-move power and close the gaps: assign/verify per-move power values for all DQ18 strikes, then measure hitstun, recoil, stagger, fall selection/intensity, and recovery time per move; any channel that is flat or non-monotonic in power gets fixed in this cycle's scope (one channel per cycle if it splits). Acceptance probe: a per-move reaction table, monotonic in power on every measured channel.

## CORRECTION — Kev, 2026-10-26 ~11:33 CT (recorded by main agent) — SUPERSEDES DQ17j's trigger

Kev: "Not stumbling after falling. Stumbling after getting hit with the appropriate amount of force to illicit that response."

- **DQ17j as merged (cycle 41) put the stumble in the WRONG place** — after the get-up. The stumble is a STANDING HIT REACTION, not a recovery-from-fall behavior.
- **NEW TOP ITEM — DQ17k STUMBLE RELOCATION (next cycle, ahead of DQ19):**
  1. REMOVE the stumble from the get-up path: after DQ17i's gradual rise, the fighter returns cleanly to stance — no stumble, ever, after a fall.
  2. ADD the stumble to the standing hit reaction, gated by force: a standing hit whose strike power meets/exceeds the stumble threshold elicits the stumble INSTEAD of the plain hitstun/recoil. Below the threshold: proportional recoil/hitstun only (no stumble from light hits — a jab must never stagger a fighter into corrective steps). Above the knockdown/launch band: the existing fall behavior governs (the hit fells him; no standing stumble). The stumble occupies the band BETWEEN recoil and knockdown.
  3. Reuse the cycle-41 stumble machinery (COM-driven corrective steps, power-scaled duration/steps, vulnerability, stance regained at end) with the new trigger. Severity still scales with the eliciting strike's power (Kev's proportionality rule).
  4. The desperation-strike chance (~15%, measured) moves WITH the stumble to the post-hit state — same standing-recovery state, correct trigger.
  - Acceptance probe must show: (a) get-up → stance with ZERO stumble frames across knockdowns of every power; (b) standing hits below threshold → no stumble; (c) standing hits in the stumble band → stumble with COM exit/recovery and power-scaled length; (d) hits in the knockdown band → fall, no standing stumble; (e) desperation rate in band over trials.
- DQ19 (reaction proportionality audit) follows DQ17k and now also audits the stumble threshold band per move.

## DQ25 ADOPTED + NEW STANDING PROGRAM DQ26 — POSITION-ORIGIN STRIKES (Kev direct, 2026-10-27 ~01:18 CT)
Kev's verdict on the DQ25 candidate: "Ok yea that stance is perfect." — DQ25 is ACCEPTED. NEW STANDING PROGRAM — DQ26 POSITION-ORIGIN STRIKES (Kev direct, 2026-10-27 ~01:18 CT): "We'll work on having the fighting moves originate from the position the figure is already in, giving the game another element of realism — i.e. if a player is trying to strike from a low position they can only reach so far. They don't instantly snap into a position that allows that strike."
Rules for all strike work from here:
- Every strike's animation BEGINS from the fighter's actual current pose (idle stance, low stance, mid-shuffle, post-recovery) — no pose snap, root jump, or limb teleport at strike start; joint positions stay continuous frame-to-frame through the strike's first frames.
- REACH IS POSTURE-BOUND: a strike's effective reach derives from where the limb actually is + true limb extension from that position. From a low/wide stance, a strike reaches only as far as the body can extend from there; reaching a farther target requires closing distance first (shuffle/cross-step in — ties directly to DQ24 locomotion) or the strike falls short.
- Power stays logical (extends DQ19): a strike thrown from a compromised/extended position carries the power its body mechanics support — full weight transfer only when the base supports it.
Sequencing: (1) promotion cycle above; (2) DQ24 stance locomotion tuned to the ADOPTED DQ25 stance (shuffle in stance + cross-step for distance, no flashing); (3) DQ26a strike-origin audit — probe every strike for start-frame pose discontinuity and measure true reach from the DQ25 stance; fix the worst offender first, one move per cycle; (4) continue the standing expansion: more realistic martial-arts moves, fluidity passes, movement-mechanics refinement, logical power scaling — alternating with fall refinement as before. All items close only on Kev's visual verdict.

blocker analysis (recorded, not hidden): the side kick's foot travel from the DQ25 idle rear position to contact is 2.27 m in a 9-frame strike window (baseline travel from the generic centre start is only 1.62 m), and the leg must go from bent to near-full extension (1.24 m reach) inside that window. Near full extension the knee angle changes ~45 deg per frame for a 0.21 m distance step, so any foot path that reaches contact by t=9 either moves the foot too fast per frame (>0.32) or straightens the knee too fast in the final frames. This is a rig-window limitation, not a one-line tuning miss: a passing fix needs either a longer side-kick strike window, a knee-angle easing in the IK layer, or a direction+radius foot path designed around the knee-angle rate — all out of scope for a single-slice change and none attempted here. ## Kev verdict — cycle 80 side kick REJECTED on anatomy (2026-10-28 ~02:32 CT)
Kev, watching the DQ80 video: Blue's side kick "isn't anatomically correct. It looks like his foot is just being flung up towards the target. regardless of anatomy." Diagnosis confirmed in code: the DQ80 branch preserved the old DQ18e kick path byte-identical at contact and only fixed its start. The striking foot travels from idle directly to 1.24 m on a near-monotonic path (fr = [-.70+1.88*wx, 1.24*wy, ...], wy = ru^1.1) — no chamber, no hip rotation lead (rotS/rotH scale linearly with e), no support-foot pivot (lead foot slides flat), no re-chamber/plant phasing. Next cycle priority: side-kick ANATOMY REBUILD under the J-program kick rule (chamber → hip/support-foot rotation → extend → re-chamber → plant, knee leads, extension eases, peak extension at the contact frame), keeping the DQ80 origin fix (0.000 snap) and the contact pose. Cycle 80's origin change is NOT reverted unless Kev says so explicitly — reverting would restore the 0.989 start snap.

blocker analysis (recorded, not hidden): the BLUE throw is a rig-window limitation, not a tuning miss. The rear hand must travel 1.118 m absolute (1.412 m in shoulder-relative offset space) in a 5-frame startup while the shoulder rises 0.543 m, so the shoulder->hand offset must rotate ~173 deg (127 deg -> -46 deg) in 5 frames. A straight path collapses the offset to 0.101 m and flips the elbow (0.827). Any detour that keeps the offset out of the shoulder keeps the elbow quiet only by lengthening the hand path past ~1.6 m, which pushes some per-frame joint step past 0.32 — the grid search found the frontier at 0.327/0.325, 2% over. A passing fix needs one of: (a) a longer throw startup window (M.T su 5 -> longer, a mechanics change, not a slice), (b) a style-specific BLUE throw contact that stays low (pelvis near the DQ25 0.70 height instead of rising to 1.243 — a throw redesign, not an origin slice, and it would split BLUE/RED throw contacts), or (c) a direction+radius rear-hand path designed around the elbow-angle rate (the cycle-74 option (c), still unbuilt). objective: DQ98 (next per the cycle-97 next step, queue kept moving per Kev's 2026-10-27 ~19:49 lean; DQ83 throw origin stays OPEN with its documented blocker, no rig-level decision taken this cycle): DQ27c slice 1 — measure whether a LIVE sidestep/backstep actually dodges by physically leaving the strike's path or range, for every strike type, both styles, both sidestep directions, at 0.85 and 1.0 m. ONE behavior audited: defender sidestep started at the attacker's go() (D0, 0-frame reaction) or 6 frames before go (L6, step in progress at go). No code changed by design (no passing animation-scale fix was found — see STEPV sweep).
baseline mechanics (measured on b8c0412e): STEPV 3.4 m/s, step lasts 13 ticks (total displacement ~0.74 m); startup P 6f / K 9f / L 13f / T 5f; swept-tip radius P 0.41 / K 0.44, forearm segment radius 0.365, throw point radius HURT_T 0.40. A sidestep completed BEFORE go() never evades (the attacker's facing locks onto the defender's new position at go() — re-aim, not a defect); only a step still in progress at go() can evade, by travelling during startup.
direction matrix (probe_dq98_gate.cjs, D0, hp 100 = evaded, both distances unless noted): P0 evades -z only; P1 evades +z only; P2 evades -z only; P3 evades +z only; P4 RED overhand evades NEITHER direction at 0.85 or 1.0; P4 BLUE sweeping back palm evades NEITHER at 0.85, evades -z at 1.0. K0 RED evades both; K0 BLUE evades -z only; K1 RED evades +z only; K1 BLUE evades both; K2 RED evades -z only; K2 BLUE evades both. Launcher evades both directions. Throw evades NEITHER direction at either distance. Static (no-step) cases still hit for every P/T variant (no false evasion). Back-walk anticipated 13f evades P at 1.0, K1 at 1.0, launcher, and throw (grab range left by separation) — backstep is a working anticipated throw counter; reactive back-walk (D0) evades nothing. Guard still blocks P/K/L with chip (99.2/98.6/98.4) and does NOT block throw (throw beats guard, by design).
root cause (traces probe_dq98_punch_trace.cjs + probe_dq98_p4_trace.cjs): a sidestep travels only ~0.28 m before a punch's first active frame (5 defender moves at STEPV 3.4) and ~0.23 m before a throw's (4 moves), against hit radii 0.41/0.365/0.40 — and the defender orbits the attacker as its facing auto-turns, so its x-distance to the fist also grows as it sidesteps. Straight punches evade in one direction because their arm runs parallel to the strike line offset to one side; P4 fails both directions because its forearm is DIAGONAL (RED overhand elbow z -0.061 -> fist z +0.13; BLUE back palm elbow -0.062 -> fist +0.13), so the arm segment spans the centerline and a sidestepper on either side stays within 0.365 of some point on it (at 1.0 m RED P4 still hits by 0.004 on the tip test: distance 0.406 vs 0.41). Throw fails because 4 moves of travel cannot clear the 0.40 grab radius from a 0.10 starting gap.
STEPV scratch sweep (rejected, builds deleted): STEPV 4.0/4.5/5.0/5.5/6.0 in scratch only — kicks all evade from 4.5 up, but P0/P2/P4 and throw STILL hit at 6.0; throw needs ~6.5 (0.42 m in 4 moves) and P0 needs ~7.0 (forearm clearance 0.555 in z), i.e. a 1.5 m total step — absurd, and it would change every step/AI-sidestep distance in the game. A STEPV raise is therefore NOT a viable fix, and no dispatch was made for it. Fixing P4 would mean moving its elbow/fist (breaks DQ88 static gates) and fixing throw reactively would mean a balance change (throw startup 5f, or a burst step profile) — both are design decisions, not animation fixes, so per the cycle-83 precedent they are scoped for Kev's direction rather than forced this cycle.

## QUEUED BY KEV 2026-10-29 ~02:23 CT — DQ105 STYLE-SPECIFIC THROWS (grab + manipulation + toss)
Kev's question + directive, verbatim in substance: "What kind of throw is this? Depending on the style, the limbs of the thrower need to be shown grabbing the opponent and manipulating their body (ie grabbing an arm, turning them in the air, etc) and then the resulting toss."
CURRENT STATE (honest answer, build e72b2c46): the throw is a GENERIC, STYLE-AGNOSTIC LIFT-AND-TOSS, not a named technique. One shared M.T branch for both styles: thrower dip+heave (DQ103), defender anchor-carried 12 ticks (DQ104: root lift to 0.60 m, pose blended into the flight pose), release into the DQ99 ballistic arc (apex 0.88, travel 1.05). There is NO visible limb-to-limb grab (no thrower hand reaching a specific defender point and holding it), NO in-air manipulation or turn (the defender tips into the flight pose while held, then flies the arc), and NO difference between Blue (Kung Fu) and Red (Boxing).
ITEM: per-style throws built on the DQ104 carry as the base. Each style gets its own grab + manipulation + toss: the thrower's limb must visibly reach a specific opponent point (e.g. arm/wrist), hold contact through the manipulation phase, manipulate the defender's body (e.g. turn them in the air), and only then release into the toss. Acceptance (probe BEFORE dispatch): grab-point tracking — thrower hand to defender target point stays small through grab + manipulation (no anchor-only carry, no teleport); defender rotation measured during the manipulation phase; no snap (DQ27b fluidity standard); damage/reach/contact unchanged except where the acted motion requires it; every other strike byte-identical; full match completes; park fix intact; normal + slow-mo video. DQ99 arc family stays as the flight phase unless the style's toss requires its own arc. TECHNIQUE PER STYLE OPEN: Kev to name or approve a proposal (standing proposal: Blue Kung Fu = arm grab + turn in the air + toss; Red Boxing = clinch + hip/body toss). QUEUE HEAD for cycle 105, ahead of DQ83 and DQ27c (DQ27c still blocked on Kev's sidestep question).

## DQ105 TECHNIQUES APPROVED (Kev, 2026-10-29 ~02:25 CT)
Kev on the standing proposal: "Those are good." Techniques are SET, no longer open: BLUE (Kung Fu) = arm grab + turn the opponent in the air + toss; RED (Boxing) = clinch + hip/body toss. Cycle 105 builds DQ105 with these techniques under the acceptance criteria in the QUEUED entry above.

## Kev video reference — SEOI NAGE VARIATIONS — 2026-10-29 ~11:15 CT (direct, main chat)
Kev sent YouTube "Variations of Shoulder throw - Seoi nage / Seoi Otoshi / Ippon Seoi Nage" (Daniel Pyatt, 9:19) with "Try this throw." Browser watch completed 11:37 CT (no sign-in/download). Breakdown: (1) seoi nage "half shoulder" ~1:47 — one-arm trap/block, standing 180-degree turn-in, back-to-chest, opponent pulled only halfway over, lands at thrower's side, lock follow-up. (2) ippon seoi nage "full shoulder" ~2:20 — same trapped-arm setup, full commitment, opponent travels all the way over in a full forward arc, lands in front. (3) crude arm-break ~3:06 — one arm seized and snapped over the top, body dragged after. (4) grip variants ~3:49 — hand-over-arm lift, elbow-lock variant, threaded arm with kuzushi only. (5) seoi otoshi "shoulder drop" ~4:47 — two hands on lapels, turn-in + drop to one/both knees, lower vertical lift, opponent drops in front. Instructor's distinction: intent (lock vs pure throw) + arc (half vs full over); naming varies by dojo. These are arm-trap turn-in throws, DISTINCT from the DQ108 back-carry drape shoulder throw (still harness-only/unbound). Variation choice pending Kev's pick; build queues on his word.

## KEV THROW SEQUENCE DIRECTIVE — 2026-10-29 ~18:43 CT (direct, governs the seoi rework)
"When throwing, the figure needs to start by pulling in the other players arm, positioning his body in front of his, bending over and tossing the other player forward over his shoulder into the ground. Get that as accurate as possible." Governing sequence for the ippon seoi nage rework, in order: (1) PULL IN the opponent's arm (grip/pull first, not a simultaneous grab); (2) POSITION the thrower's body IN FRONT of the opponent's (step/turn-in placing the thrower in front, back against the opponent); (3) BEND OVER (thrower bends forward under the load); (4) TOSS the opponent FORWARD over the shoulder INTO THE GROUND (full forward arc, landing on the ground in front). Supersedes the looser DQ120 "full motion" framing as the acceptance spec; the DQ120 elbow-flip fix remains required within this rework. Style binding + reach/damage still OPEN until the motion is right. This sequence is seoi-specific (pull-arm + body-in-front + bend + forward-over-shoulder toss) and does not re-spec the DQ108 back-carry drape.

## KEV 12-MINUTE AUTO-DECIDE RULE — 2026-10-29 ~18:45 CT (direct, governing)
"If you don't get a verdict from me, make a decision and improve upon it within 12 minutes of release." RULE: every cycle release starts a 12-minute clock. If no Kev verdict is recorded within 12 minutes of release, Muse DECIDES the item itself (accept, rework direction, or defect disposition) and dispatches the improvement — no more validation-only cycles stalling on an awaited verdict. Implementation: each delivery carries its release time; a follow-up check at +12 min acts when no verdict landed; cycle workers treat any release >12 min old with no recorded verdict as decided-by-Muse. Decisions under this rule stay revertible on Kev's word, as under the 2026-10-27 delegation. ## KEV-SUPPLIED REFERENCE — ARM-PULL THROW RIG — 2026-10-30 ~08:09 CT
owner: Kev | file: files/dojo-arm-throw-rig-reference-20261030.html (copy of user upload dojo_arm_throw_rig.html)
mechanism (engine-agnostic, pure function of time, 2D side view, meters, +y up): victim's gripped wrist is PINNED to the thrower's hand; when the arm goes taut (wrist-to-shoulder distance > arm length 0.78 m), the victim's WHOLE BODY is dragged by that arm (pinArm) — this is the visible "pulled over the shoulder by the arm" read. Victim torso stays upright during pull-in, then rotates around the thrower's shoulder (spine angle 0 → -0.12 → -0.55 → -1.6 → -2.5 at release t=1.12). Thrower drops under (pelvis 0.66, bow 0.35 at t=0.55), drives up and bows 0.80–0.95 at release. Events: grab t=0.15, release t=1.12, impact with hitstop 0.09 + shake 0.5. Flight baked (gravity 14, tossSpeed 2.2) so landing is exact, with bounce settle. Demo viewer: scrubbable, 1x/0.5x/0.25x, phase label (reach / pull-in-turn / lift-&-toss arm-pull / flight / landed), gold grip dot while gripped.
standing treatment: REFERENCE + refactor scope only, NOT a wholesale import — the live VF engine is pose-table based, not a time-function rig. Next ippon rework briefs from this mechanism: pin the gripped wrist to the thrower's hand through the pull, let arm-tautness drag the victim's body over the shoulder, keep the torso upright until the shoulder rotation begins.

## KEV THROW DIRECTIVE — VICTIM FACING FLIP + FORWARD FLIGHT + NO INVERSION — 2026-10-30 ~15:43 CT
owner: Kev | developer: next cycle (142) queue head — supersedes the cycle-141 "arm-dip geometry" next item
verbatim: "The figure being thrown should go from facing left to right after being positioned for the throw. Once thrown that figure should fly forward over the throwing figures shoulder. At no point should he turn upside down when being grabbed or going through the motion of being thrown"
read as three acceptance rules for the ippon sequence:
  (1) FACING FLIP: during the positioning phase the victim's facing reverses left→right, BEFORE the toss, so the toss direction reads as his forward.
  (2) FORWARD FLIGHT: once tossed, the victim flies FORWARD over the thrower's shoulder (translational arc in the throw direction).
  (3) NO INVERSION, FULL SEQUENCE: the victim never turns upside down at any point — not while grabbed, not during positioning/manipulation, and not through the throw motion itself. This TIGHTENS the Oct 30 ~13:41 rule (which allowed rotation/flip in the toss/flight itself): under this directive the flight arc is translational, not rotational. If Kev intended the toss arc itself to still rotate, he will correct this read live.
next cycle must measure: victim facing angle through positioning (left→right flip before release), flight path direction (forward over shoulder), and inversion across the ENTIRE sequence (head-below-pelvis / inverted ticks = 0 through grab, positioning, throw, and flight), and the video must show the full sequence at normal + slow-mo.

change attempted (ISOLATED, all rejected, record-only in builds/): (1) feet easing carryK + 0.15*sin(pi*uu/(11/12)), zero at vicT11 — Blue kr 0.278 -> 0.260 m, Red kr 0.379 -> 0.359 m, but Red segment dev 0.416 -> 0.504 m. (2) feet + knee-blend easing — Red kr worsens to 0.430-0.490 m. (3) turn/pitch rotation hold (factor 1 - 0.5*((carryK-0.5)/0.5)^2 after peak, 0.545 retained at last carry tick vs 0.072 live) — Blue carry improves but creates a release snap at first air tick (head 0.356 m, fr 0.352 m) because shipped air poses do NOT blend from airFrom (that blend is ippon-only); Red kr barely moves (0.379 -> 0.382 m). All variants: grip at release, flight 21 ticks, apex 0.88, touchdown 36, ippon forced runs unchanged.
tests: contact probe (6 runs) on live + all variants — PASS as measurement, NOT PROMOTABLE for any variant (diff gate vs live fails). Range/rapid/replay/authority/full-match/park-fix NOT RUN on rejected variants (probe hard failure disqualifies; flight/touchdown/grip-at-release identical to live). Ten checks on live: 2 joint-snapping FAIL (known shipped flags, unchanged), 3 limb lengths PARTIAL (pre-existing segment devs), 7 throw-specific PASS (genuine G+P, both directions, full grip->recovery, HP 100 -> 78). Genuine gameplay inputs: YES (video uses real press('g') + press('p'), both directions, live build). Device test: NOT RUN (Kev-gated).
result: BLOCKED/ESCALATED (no candidate presented as a fix; live preserved byte-identical). Easing/holding any single carry element either barely moves the Red peak or trades it for a worse failure (segment dev, release snap). Beating the 0.20 m gate honestly requires changing carry targets AND the flight starting pose together — a re-authored launch pose, a gameplay-visible change needing Kev's call.
next step: Kev's call: (a) authorise a joint carry+flight re-authoring (changing the launch pose), (b) re-scope the 0.20 m gate for the carry window, or (c) accept the live carry knee/foot peaks as known open defects (and, separately, the 163 grip gains with the knee peak open). 163 stays HELD. No candidate is presented this cycle.
